expected.title: The Difference is Real: local vs systematic scope (V3-I)

review_note.NOT_AMBIGUITY: This is NOT a genuine 'two meanings' ambiguity. The two readings are different INFERENTIAL STRENGTHS: Reading A is LOCALLY ENTAILED (this passage refutes the anirvācya-ignorance thesis); Reading B is a CONTEXTUALLY SUPPORTED EXTENSION (difference as the self's manifestation) that relies on broader doctrine (V3-G/H, V2-S). The crux is not 'which reading is true' but: does THIS passage itself license the positive metaphysical interpretation, or does that require importing the broader doctrine?
review_note.SUPPORT_SCOPE_FIRST_CLASS: This gold case is exactly the kind that forces support_scope (LOCAL_TEXT / LOCAL_CONTEXT / SAME_WORK / CROSS_WORK / SYSTEMATIC_RECONSTRUCTION) to be considered first-class in the IR — not yet added to the ontology, but flagged.

expected.research_question: What does 'the difference is real' mean — does the passage positively affirm difference as the self's manifestation, or negatively establish it by refuting the 'un-explainable ignorance' thesis?

nodes.text: If consciousness is one and the difference of things is mere ignorance, how is action possible — for action needs a distinct agent and object?
nodes.boundary: the objection presupposes that a unified consciousness leaves no distinct object for action

nodes.text: The single re-recollection marked by the will-to-do (cikīrṣālakṣaṇa parāmarśa) joins the agent and the object; action is possible in the one consciousness.
nodes.derived_from: L2 (the will-to-do joins agent and object)

nodes.text: The difference cannot be an 'un-explainable' (anirvācya) ignorance: of whom would it be? The one-form reality cannot have it; the separate souls cannot bear it; 'un-explainable' is a refusal to answer.
nodes.boundary: this refutes the illusion-thesis; it does not by itself give the positive account of difference

nodes.text: The difference is real — cognition rests in difference as it does not rest in non-difference.
nodes.boundary: Reading A: difference-real = the illusion thesis is refuted; NOT a full positive metaphysics of difference

nodes.text: The difference is real as the self's own manifestation — the positive account of difference (developed in V3-G/H, V2-S).
nodes.derivation: SYSTEMATIC_INTERPRETATION (NOT a local inference from G5-TC1+G5-TC2)
nodes.boundary: Reading B: difference-real = the self's own manifestation; the full positive account is developed elsewhere (V3-G/H, V2-S)

inferences.rationale: The 'un-explainable ignorance' account collapses (G5-TC2) — so the difference is real in the sense of not being mere ignorance (G5-CONC-A).

boundary.text: The passage establishes that the difference cannot be an 'un-explainable' (anirvācya) ignorance. Whether 'the difference is real' is read negatively (refuting the illusion thesis) or positively (difference as the self's manifestation) is a genuine crux — two defensible reconstructions. The full positive account of the difference is developed elsewhere (V3-G/H, V2-S).
not_claiming: a full positive metaphysics of difference (developed elsewhere)
that absolute monism with ignorance is endorsed (the passage is not an absolute monism either)
that Reading A and Reading B contradict one another

debate_frame.question: What does 'the difference is real' mean — does the passage positively affirm difference as the self's manifestation, or negatively establish it by refuting the 'un-explainable ignorance' thesis?
debate_frame.object_of_dispute: the force of 'the difference is real' in V3-I
shared_ground: the difference cannot be dismissed as anirvācya ignorance
action is the one will-to-do joining agent and object
disputed_ground: whether 'the difference is real' is a negative (refutation) or positive (self-manifestation) claim

positions.label: Reading A — MINIMAL / LOCAL
positions.question: What does the passage itself establish?
positions.commitment: the difference is real = the illusion/ignorance thesis is refuted (locally entailed)

positions.label: Reading B — STRONGER / SYSTEMATIC
positions.question: What stronger interpretation becomes supportable with wider corpus context?
positions.commitment: the difference is real = difference is the self's own manifestation (contextually supported extension)

semantic_alignments.rationale: anirvācya = 'that which cannot be spoken of'; the C1 treats it as a refusal to answer (yakṣa-speech)
Both readings affirm difference is real; they differ in the MODE — A = refuted-illusion status, B = the self's manifestation. Overlapping, not contradictory.
CONC-A answers 'what does the passage refute'; CONC-B answers 'what does it positively affirm'. Same shared ground, different question — NOT a VIRUDDHA (opposition) pair.
